newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power deregulation stumbles on stranded costs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power deregulation stumbles on stranded costs.

text.p: Stranded costs, the huge debts assumed by utilities to fund past power projects, were singled out by industry officials meeting here Friday as one of the biggest roadblocks to a free North American power market.

The stakes are high - at least $300 billion in the U.S. - and deciding who will pay is a major obstacle to deregulation, William Poist, head of Massachusetts' Commonwealth Energy System, told a Canada-U.S. energy trade conference.
"(The electric industry) is still in the denial/crisis phase, and one reason we are lagging is stranded cost," said Stephen Chesebro, head of Tenneco Energy, a unit of Tenneco Inc.
